visual_action: A montage of grainy, historical footage of pro-choice protests from a past era, including shots of the White House, is contrasted with modern, color footage of a large, contemporary pro-choice protest march. Protesters in both eras carry signs advocating for abortion rights. The final shot shows a protester holding a sign in front of the Supreme Court building.

cast.name: Democratic Party
cast.evidence: The video was posted by the official @democrats account.

on_screen_text.text: Abortion a woman's right to choose

spoken_summary: The video contains no spoken words, only song lyrics from "A Man Without Love."
audio_music: The video begins with the slow, romantic song "A Man Without Love" by Engelbert Humperdinck over historical footage. After about 6 seconds, a harsh record-scratch sound effect cuts the music, and a more upbeat, driving section of the same song begins, playing over modern protest footage for an energetic and defiant effect.
editing_pacing: The video is a montage with a distinct shift in pace. It starts with slower cuts of historical footage and transitions abruptly to faster, more energetic cuts of modern protest scenes.
cultural_references: The song "A Man Without Love" by Engelbert Humperdinck
The song 'Truth Hurts' by Lizzo, referenced on a protest sign.
The Gadsden flag ('Don't Tread on Me') design, adapted with a uterus image for a protest sign.
central_claim: The fight for abortion rights is a long-standing, multi-generational struggle that continues with renewed energy and defiance in the present day.
intended_effect: To energize and mobilize supporters of abortion rights by connecting their current activism to a historical movement and showing the strength of contemporary protests.
